findings.failure_mode: Tasks that call self.retry() while the broker is briefly unable to accept publishes are lost for good. They end up in FAILURE with a kombu OperationalError instead of being retried. On-call sees a burst of task-failed events and FAILURE results naming connection or publish errors, and that work never runs again.
findings.trigger_condition: Publishing the retry message fails for longer than the default task_publish_retry_policy window (3 retries at 0/0.2/0.4s, so roughly 0.6s), while the worker can still reject or ack the original message. Examples: a RabbitMQ node failover, a memory or disk alarm that blocks publishers but not consumers, or a Redis failover.
findings.amplifier: Retries cluster when a downstream dependency is failing, and that is also when broker trouble tends to coincide. Every task that hits retry() inside the window turns into Reject(requeue=False). The original message is acked or rejected without a requeue, so nothing redelivers it.
findings.blast_radius: Every in-flight task type that uses manual retry() on the affected workers. Chords and chains that contain those tasks fail through their errbacks instead of completing.

evidence.note: S.apply_async() failure is turned into Reject(exc, requeue=False): no requeue and no fallback
Reject without requeue is recorded as a terminal FAILURE and the message is rejected without requeue
default publish retry policy gives up after about 0.6s across 3 attempts

findings.confidence_rationale: The loss path is explicit in the code and confirmed in request.py. No [fix] commit in the bundle touches retry(), so the ceiling is medium. I did not observe the trigger, and whether a blocked publish raises or hangs depends on kombu and the transport.
findings.how_to_verify: Under a worker with acks_late, make Producer.publish raise OperationalError for 2s, for example with a toxiproxy cut on the publish connection only. Run a task that calls self.retry(countdown=1). The task ends in FAILURE and is never re-executed, and the queue holds no retry message.
findings.prediction: The next broker failover incident includes reports of retried tasks marked FAILURE with connection errors that never ran again

findings.failure_mode: After a downstream outage, every task that failed during it comes back at the same moment, default_retry_delay (180s) or one fixed countdown later. The dependency sees periodic synchronized spikes, so it fails again when it should be recovering, and tasks use up max_retries (default 3) and fail permanently.
findings.trigger_condition: A shared dependency such as an API or database is unavailable for a short time while many tasks are in flight. Each task calls self.retry() with no countdown or a constant one.
findings.amplifier: The countdown is used as-is, with no jitter and no growth per attempt. N failures inside the outage window become N retries landing inside the same short window.
findings.sustaining_effect: Retry waves stay in phase: tasks that fail in wave k all reschedule together for wave k+1. Each wave pushes the recovering dependency back over capacity until max_retries runs out, so the outage outlasts its trigger by up to max_retries x countdown.
findings.blast_radius: Every caller of the shared dependency, not only Celery workers, sees the load spikes every 180s. Tasks that use up their retries are lost as FAILURE.

evidence.note: countdown falls back to the fixed default_retry_delay, with no jitter or backoff in manual retry()
the countdown is passed unchanged into the retry signature

findings.confidence_rationale: The code clearly has no jitter. autoretry_for with retry_backoff and retry_jitter exists elsewhere for users who opt in, so the impact depends on how callers use manual retry(). There is no fix history for it in the bundle.
findings.how_to_verify: Enqueue 1,000 tasks that all fail against a stub returning 503 for 10s and call self.retry(). Plot the ETA distribution of the retry messages. They fall inside a window of about 10s at t+180s instead of being spread out.

notes: The replace() chain-with-group area has had two fixes in a row (01608ff, 8aed820). I checked canvas _chain.from_dict: deserialized chain tasks are turned back into signatures, so the isinstance(group) check holds and I could not confirm a remaining failure. In apply(), eager retry recurses through retval.sig.apply(retries=retries+1) at line 961 and ignores countdown. With max_retries=None that ends in RecursionError, but it only applies to eager mode, so I mentioned it here rather than reporting it. 72a968d (the apply_async options copy) looks correct. The bundle had no detector leads. Files: <celery>/celery/app/task.py, <celery>/celery/worker/request.py, <celery>/celery/app/defaults.py.
